deltas.status: residual verification closed; no substantive clean-text reversal
deltas.secure_text: To R.D.'s remark it shld be added ... the central point wh. it makes, the point whereon its 'doctrine of release' is based is the separateness of the Self & the World, — in a word its thorough-going dualism. A more likely reference to a genuinely Sankhyan doctrine is ... Majjhima-Nikaya Sutta 63: 'the soul is one thing & the body is another' etc.
deltas.editorial_consequence: Closes the former p.17 punctuation/location blind spot. The page explicitly shifts evidential weight from generic eternity-of-matter/self resemblance to the separateness/dualism relation.

deltas.status: argument structure upgraded; no verbatim publication quotation yet
deltas.witness_status: W3 for the central distinction; W2 for several connecting words
deltas.secure_text: But what is meant by moral notions? ... when we find the rich in the next life are still rich, we cannot call this continuance a case of recompense for virtue.
deltas.editorial_consequence: Lovejoy separates mere continuity of status from moral recompense. Afterlife difference becomes moral only when it is tied to conduct/desert rather than persistence of terrestrial rank or capacity.

deltas.witness_status: W3 for the anti-moral inference and quasi-mechanical contrast; some wording remains W2
deltas.secure_text: No more again can religious devotion be held to imply an idea of a moral sort ... [the relation can be] in a purely quasi-mechanical manner.
deltas.editorial_consequence: Ritual success/reward is explicitly separated from moral judgment. A practice may generate an afterlife consequence through a quasi-mechanical religious relation without constituting moral eschatology.

deltas.witness_status: W3 for the closing historical characterization
deltas.secure_text: [The other world] is not properly a copy of the present world of today but of yesterday; the morality supposed to be reigning there is commonly a little traditional & obsolete.
deltas.editorial_consequence: The afterlife is treated as a lagging historical layer, preserving older norms rather than transparently mirroring the present.

deltas.status: source-critical memorandum merged into clean batch
deltas.secure_text: Tylor, the master of t. school Anthropolog'y, + t. only one wh. does not construct theories beyond his evidence. his bks shld always be kept at hand in study of subject.
deltas.editorial_consequence: Direct notebook evidence that Lovejoy ranks authorities partly by refusal to construct theories beyond evidence; this is a source-critical norm, not merely an inferred trait of his later practice.

deltas.status: mechanism upgrade merged into clean batch
deltas.secure_text: the sacrifice is merely a means of magical compulsion, as it were purely mechanical ... a charm wh. directly controls natural phenomena ... often t. god is not concerned in it at all
deltas.editorial_consequence: A sacrifice can operate through direct quasi-mechanical efficacy rather than divine will; visible sacrificial form does not identify the operative relation.

deltas.status: argument/transcription upgrade merged into clean batch
deltas.witness_status: W3 for 'not ritual but alimentary', male-flesh preference, and gastronomic contrast
deltas.secure_text: Cannibalism ... not ritual but alimentary ... [preference for male flesh despite a stated gastronomic superiority of female flesh].
deltas.editorial_consequence: Lovejoy treats the base practice as alimentary while using selective preference to test modification by non-alimentary ideas about power/value. This is an anti-form control: ceremonial/selective consumption is not automatically sacrifice or sacrament.

deltas.status: substantive directionality correction merged into clean batch
deltas.witness_status: W3 for H.S. -> domestic-animal-sacrifice direction; compressed middle wording W2
deltas.secure_text: [The] manner of the H.S. is in turn modified into sacr. of dom. an., dressed as a man & so on. The dom. an. sac. ... comes not fr. wild an. sac. directly, but by modification of H.S. ...
deltas.withdraw: former clean summary: 'sacrifice of domestic animals can be modified into sacrifice of a divine animal or divine representative'
deltas.replace_with: Lovejoy is testing a substitutional/developmental direction in which human sacrifice (H.S.) is modified into domestic-animal sacrifice, including animals dressed/treated in human fashion; he explicitly denies that this domestic-animal form need derive directly from wild-animal sacrifice.
deltas.editorial_consequence: This reverses the causal direction in the first-pass summary. The page belongs with p.103 as a sequence-testing exercise: proposed ritual succession is decomposed into alternative historical pathways rather than one linear wild-animal -> domestic-animal story.
